slides.say: A, B and C represent digits. Given: B C A, plus B C, is equal to A A A. C is equal to what?
So an addition again, and they ask only for C. [short pause] We'll solve it with the four steps. First, vertically.
The leftmost digit? A three-digit number plus a two-digit number, and the sum still has three digits. No new digit, so the rule about one doesn't help here.
So the ones column. A plus C ends in A. Nothing carries into the ones, so adding C changed nothing. C is zero. Choice number two is our answer.

slides.say: And it's real. With nothing carried, the tens give B equal to A. Three hundred three plus thirty is three hundred thirty-three, and four hundred four plus forty is four hundred forty-four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
